QF.id: AIFM Fee Structure and Fund Performance_36

question.text: Category I and Category II AIFs must be structured as ________ per SEBI AIF Regulations because their underlying investments are primarily illiquid.

answer.text: Listed closed-end funds with mandatory stock exchange listing

explanation.text: **The Logic:** Ch 9.4.1 Point 2: Cat I and II AIFs must be CLOSE-ENDED because investments are primarily illiquid. Cat III can be open or close ended. **The Trap:** Option B violates the illiquidity match. Option C is not a mandate. Option D is an MF concept. **Cross-Exam Context:** XIX-A tests this directly; XIX-C requires the manager to match fund structure to strategy. **Manager's Pro-Tip:** Close-ended structure fixes LP capital for fund life — plan extensions (typically 2x1-year) in the PPM. Early redemption via LP secondary sales requires GP consent — draft the transfer process carefully.
